Rising is the ability to maintain hand height and apply back pressure, relying on radial deviation and elbow flexion. A strong riser keeps the knuckles high, but a fully cupped wrist eliminates this advantage. Ermes Gasparini’s riser has been stronger than Devon Larratt’s, but his lack of wrist flexion limited its effectiveness.  

Devon excels in maintaining height, using back pressure and hand control to dominate setups. Posting toprollers avoid deep cupping to preserve their riser, while low hand toprollers counter wrist flexion by targeting the pinky side.  

The King’s Move depends on pronation, **riser**, and arm locks, starting from full supination for structural support. Some argue that banning it would harm the sport.  

While some arm wrestlers train their riser directly, others develop it through exercises like hammer curls. The debate continues on whether dedicated **riser** training is necessary or if it naturally develops through arm wrestling.

description:
I am not saying the exercise is performed incorrectly, nor am I bringing down the athletes, my point is simply that comparing armwrestling lifts isn't as simple as just comparing the weight on the pulley. How you lift weight matters, the different angles and leverage matter. The carry-over to the armwrestling table matters most: are you actually doing something useful? If you think I'm saying Ermes or Levan are weak/bad athletes, you didn't understand the past few videos.

Keep in mind there are exercises that you post on social media, and there are others you don't. Just because your favorite athlete is performing a lift doesn't mean you should too. Be critical of what you see and how you choose to train. Enhanced athletes with 20+ years of experience should not train the same way as an armwrestling beginner would.

Furthermore, there is a lot more to these lifts than just elbow flexion. title: Devon Larratt's Insane Pronation Strength
description:
In outside style arm wrestling, Pronation is the main route to a pin; to picture this, think of what a king’s move is – full on Pronation while giving up some cup.

For inside style armwrestling, having a stronger bronator than your opponent means that your hand will be on top of your opponent’s hand in a hook for instance. 

This gives you way more leverage, efficiency, and isolates their bicep even more, which makes your game far easier.

The Pronator is very important in arm wrestling. Some athletes have centered their whole style around it, like Matt Mask, Vitaly, and others.

Cupping and Pronating are two sides of the same coin. Cupping gives better leverage for you personally, and Pronating decreases the cupping of the opponent so they get worse leverage.


Devon has a very strong Pronation, even if he loses his cup, the Pronation still there.
